newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed Index 129.0 in Oct vs 129.6 in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed Index 129.0 in Oct vs 129.6 in Sept.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago on Wednesday said its Chicago Fed Midwest Manufacturing Index (CFMMI) declined to 129.0 in October from a revised 129.6 in September.
Auto-parts plant closings, resulting from a strike, largely caused the decline, the Chicago Fed's report said.
"The impact of that strike can be clearly seen in an 8.0 percent decline in auto assemblies in October," it said.
Effects of the strike may cause another decline in output for November, the report said.
The automobile component of the index dipped to 136.0 from 138.6 the month before, and the steel component fell to 128.9 from 130.0.
Both the machinery and resources components rose, to 144.3 from 144.0 and to 121.0 from 120.8, respectively.
When seasonally adjusted, the overall CFMMI slipped 0.4 percent in October, the Chicago Fed said.
